To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the finite size of the tip of an atomic force microscopy (AFM) probe can significantly affect measured AFM profiles of the upper boundary of a columnar thin film (CTF), and (b) the influence of this effect on the measured AFM profiles can be reduced by applying a surface reconstruction procedure.
the linear dimensions of columns in columnar thin films must be larger than the linear dimensions of an AFM tip in order to get reliable results.

the atomic force microscopy measurements of the real columnary thin films are affected by a strong misrepresentation of the profiles and their statistical characteristics, especially when the linear dimensions (heights, diameters) of the columns are comparable with linear dimensions of the atomic force microscope tip.
In summary, our research is concerned with
theoretical analysis of the atomic-force microscopy characterization of columnnar thin films.
the analysis of atomic force microscope measurements of columnar thin film surfaces.
the theoretical analysis of atomic force microscopy characterization and reconstruction of columnar thin film profiles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the atomic force microscopy is not a suitable method to determine the upper boundary profile of columnar thin film structures.

, for the case of columnar thin film, the atomic force microscopy technique can be successfully applied for the characterization of the columnar thin films only when the linear dimensions (heights and diameters) of the columns are larger than the linear dimensions of an AFM tip.
the atomic force microscopy technique is a useful tool to characterize the columnar thin films but the measured results have to be corrected (improved) using the surface reconstruction procedure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the finite dimensions of the atomic force microscope tip influence the measured profiles and their statistical properties.

the results of the theoretical analysis presented in this paper can be used as a basis for the development of the methods for correction of the measured profiles and their statistical characteristics.
the atomic force microscopy can be successfully used to study the real thin film structures if the linear dimensions of these structures are much larger than the linear dimensions of an AFM tip.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface reconstruction procedure can be applied to improve the accuracy of atomic force microscopy studies.
the finite size of the AFM tip can lead to significant errors in the characterization of columnar structures, which can be reduced by using surface reconstruction.
one should be very careful when interpreting the results of atomic force microscopy studies, especially in the cases of columnar thin film structures.
